texts.facts: RR Gold Tobacco 20 packets 5. Miraj- 5 packets 6. Baba 160 - 25 boxes 7. Swagath Tobacco - 50 boxes 8. Amber Tobacco - 60 boxes 5. Learned counsel for the petitioners have made a grievance that despite the notification being stayed by the Supreme Court, yet the petitioners are being harassed by the local Dr.CSL,J Crl.P.No.6774 of 2021 and batch police authorities by interfering with their day- to-day businesses.
texts.arguments: Learned counsels appearing for respective petitioners in all the cases made a common submission that this Court has disposed of batches of cases regarding the same subject matter, extensively dealing with the provisions of law invoked and also the applicability of Cigarettes and Dr.CSL,J Crl.P.No.6774 of 2021 and batch other Tobacco Products Act, 2003 and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the proceedings as the provisions of law invoked are not applicable and hence the present Criminal Petitions may be disposed of on the similar lines. 6. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor also made a submission that a similar order may be passed in these cases also. 7. Dealing with Criminal Petition No.9062 of 2021 and batch, this Court through common order dated 14.07.2022, dealing with the applicability of Cigarettes and Tobacco Products Act, 2003, at paras 16 and 17 held as follows: "16. Though as rightly projected by the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor, the use of cigarettes and allied tobacco products is injurious to health and there is every need to adopt stringent approach for curtailing the said use by the public, to prohibit production, transportation and sale of those products, there is no specific provision in the COTP Act, 2003, which makes such production, transportation and sale of the tobacco products a prohibited offence. It is not out of place to mention that for treatment of tobacco related diseases, the victims and their families are laying their lives and there are more than eight lakhs causalities every year in the country due to direct or indirect use of tobacco related products which includes cigarettes, chaini, gutkha, etc. Also, it is estimated that loss of productivity Shaik Saida vs The State Of Telangana on 31 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144995393/ 3 due to use of these products is almost Rs.13,500/- crores annually. That means, the revenue generated through the tobacco industry is worthless in the light of the annual causalities and loss of productivity due to use of those products. 17. Article 47 of the Constitution of India casts a duty upon the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people. It also states that the State should take steps for improvement of public health as the same is its primary duty. It also lays down that the State shall endeavour to bring about prohibition of consumption of intoxicating drinks which are injurious to health. This provision is under Part- IV of the Constitution of India which lays down the Directive principles of State Policy. It says that only when package of the products does not contain the label as prescribed, then the possessors of those products would be held liable for punishment. It further covers the circumstances where the said products are being sold to any person who is below the age of 18 years or that they are sold within a radius of 100 yards from any educational institution. 8. The Court in the aforementioned case also dealt with the applicability of different provisions of Indian Penal Code as arrayed in these Criminal Petitions and gave a Dr.CSL,J Crl.P.No.6774 of 2021 and batch finding with regard to their applicability at para 46 of the Order. No legislation is brought to the notice of this court to show that possession of tobacco products viz., gutka and alike and involving in the business of selling those products is banned and committing such acts is declared as disobedience to order duly promulgated by a public servant, or that the acts committed would amounts to public nuisance or those acts are likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life, or noxious for consumption as food or drink whose sale is prohibited, or that possession of tobacco products makes the atmosphere noxious to health, or there was an attempt to administer those products to any person with an intention to cause hurt, or that those acts amounts to rashly or negligently endangering life or personal safety of others or amounts to criminal breach of trust or cheating. Therefore, the provisions invoked viz., Sections 188, 269, Shaik Saida vs The State Of Telangana on 31 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144995393/ 4 270, 272, 273, 278, 328 read with 511, 336, 409 and 420 IPC does not attract to the Dr.CSL,J Crl.P.No.6774 of 2021 and batch bundle of facts that are projected by the investigating agency." 9. Further more, though the Government of Telangana issued notification vide notification No.501/FSS/I/2022, on 07.01.2022, prohibiting manufacturing, storing, distribution, transportation and sale of gutka and pan masala in the entire state of Telangana, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case between Shri Venkateshwara Traders Vs. State of Telangana and others, vide SLA No.20441 of 2021 with SLP(C).No.1656 of 2022, stayed operation of the said notification.
